title: Customer Network Handover Playbook — Audit & Approval Scenarios (Draft)
content:
Purpose
This playbook is a working PRD-style artifact to standardize the customer-managed network (VPC) handover for Private deployments. It focuses on two operational risk vectors that repeatedly surface in trials: audit fidelity for security/compliance, and approval gates that teams must pass before production cutover. The intent is pragmatic: produce a repeatable checklist, a minimal audit event taxonomy, and approval gate definitions that SRE/Product/SEs can adopt during onboarding.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments where the customer provides network infrastructure (VPC/subnets, peers, NAT, transit gateways).
- Covers audit log instrumenting, storage/retention recommendations, and the decision gates for sign-off.
- Does NOT cover low-level kernel tuning, customer-side IAM configurations beyond network-level roles, or on-prem air-gapped deployment steps (these belong in a separate ops doc).

Audience
- Solutions Engineering (lead handover)
- Customer Infra/Network engineers
- Product & SRE reviewers (approval gate approvers)
- Security/Compliance contacts for audit acceptance

Assumptions
- Customer will run control plane in their VPC or provide a VPC peering/PrivateLink endpoint depending on the chosen private model.
- We have initial network reachability validated by connectivity tests before this playbook is used.
- Customer accepts our recommended retention windows and export formats, or provides alternate compliance requirements to be captured as deviations.

High-level flow (phases)
1) Intake & Discovery — collect topology, critical subnets, ingress/egress paths, existing logging pipelines, and compliance constraints.
2) Baseline enablement — enable debug-level connectivity tests, temporary verbose audit capture for first 72 hours of integration.
3) Audit sampling & schema validation — verify event fidelity, correlate with customer logs.
4) Approval gate runbook — checklist of conditions for canary -> prod cutover.
5) Handover & retention setup — finalize long-term log exports, retention, SLA, and handover notes.

Event taxonomy (minimal required audit events)
- NETWORK_FLOW (required): timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, src_port, dst_port, protocol, path_id (if transit gateway), action (allowed/denied), rule_id, flow_bytes. Purpose: tie L7 model requests to raw network flows for forensic traces.
- CONTROL_PLANE_AUTH (required): timestamp, user_or_service, action (token-refresh, create-cred, revoke-cred), success/failure, src_ip, request_id. Purpose: capture credential lifecycle events that could affect access to runtime.
- DEPLOYMENT_ACTION (required): timestamp, actor, model_id, image_id, rollout_type (canary/blue-green), target_nodes, rollup_status. Purpose: link model rollout to infra changes.
- CONFIG_CHANGE (recommended): timestamp, actor, change_summary, change_diff_id, affected_components. Purpose: track config drift that may affect auditing or performance.
- SYS_ERROR (recommended): timestamp, component, error_code, short_message, correlation_id. Purpose: surface systemic problems during onboarding.

Notes on fidelity levels
- Level 0 (minimal): only aggregated allow/deny counts per minute per VPC — OK for non-regulated customers.
- Level 1 (for typical enterprise): full NETWORK_FLOW events + CONTROL_PLANE_AUTH with 90d retention.
- Level 2 (for regulated workloads): full events + 365d retention, signed integrity (HMAC) on batches, and streaming to customer-managed SIEM via TLS mutual auth.

Storage & retention recommendations
- Transit architecture: push to customer S3/GCS bucket or customer SIEM. For small customers, use Redwood-managed encrypted bucket with configurable retention (default 90d).
- Export formats: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) recommended. Each record must include a version field for schema evolution.
- Export cadence: hourly batches with immediate delivery on critical events (AUTH_FAIL > threshold, SYS_ERROR critical).
- Retention matrix: Level 1 -> 90 days; Level 2 -> 365 days; aggregated metrics -> 730 days.

Approval gates matrix (definitions & owners)
- Gate A: Network Reachability Test (owner: Solutions Eng)
  - Conditions: All required ports reachable from Redwood control plane endpoints; latency < threshold; route uniqueness validated.
  - Evidence: traceroute logs, connectivity matrix CSV, screenshots of successful peering.
- Gate B: Audit Schema Validation (owner: Security/Product)
  - Conditions: Event samples demonstrate required fields present and parsable; timestamp drift < 5s for 95% of events in a 1h window.
  - Evidence: NDJSON sample file (24h), parser run output, schema conformance report.
- Gate C: Canary Workload (owner: SRE)
  - Conditions: Canary model handles target QPS for 30m without retries above 2% and P95 latency within SLO; audit events captured for canary requests.
  - Evidence: Canary metrics dashboard snapshot, audit join demonstrating correspondence between requests and flow logs.
- Gate D: Security & Compliance Signoff (owner: Customer Security / Redwood Security)
  - Conditions: Customer or Redwood security approves retention and export plan; any legal data residency constraints documented.
  - Evidence: Signed appendix or email chain.

Operational handover checklist (detailed)
- Inventory provided: VPC ID, subnets, route tables, NAT/IGW, transit gateways, security group/ACL IDs.
- Credentials: least-privilege onboarding role created and rotated; credentials in vault; expiration policy documented.
- Logging endpoints: bucket/SIEM details, auth method, sample objects validated.
- Time sync: NTP/time service verified; logs show consistent timestamps.
- Escalation contacts: customer oncall, Redwood SE, Redwood SRE, Redwood Security.
- Runbook links: link to canary run, rollback steps, and emergency teardown (all attached in linked_artifacts).

Testing and validation recipes (quick wins)
- Synthetic L7 request + packet capture correlation: issue synthetic request through customer ingress and verify at three points: NLB -> host -> flow log step.
- Auth failure flood test (non-destructive): simulate auth failures to validate immediate alerting and audit export triggers.
- Partial retention test: verify that archive lifecycle rules delete logs per policy by creating a short retention test bucket.

Open questions / risk register (items to resolve before final PRD)
- Customer SIEM integration formats and supported auth methods (mutual TLS vs. token).
- Acceptable timeline for retention modifications after cutover (policy drift management).
- Scope of integrity verification (who signs batches, Redwood or customer?).
- Performance tradeoffs: verbose audit during initial onboarding increases cost/latency — define budget cap for sample period.

Implementation notes for eng handoff
- Schema must be versioned. Use "audit_v" field. Avoid breaking changes; prefer additive fields and retire via migration.
- Provide a lightweight parser (python script) maintained in private-deployments repo that validates incoming batch samples and emits a conformance report. Link: github:repo/private-deployments#pr-214.
- Instrument correlation_id throughout the stack (API gateway -> runtime -> worker) to make canary validation straightforward.

Next steps & immediate actions (owner tags)
- SE: Run Discovery checklist with customer (this week).
- Product: Finalize Level definitions and retention defaults (two weeks).
- Security: Draft formal acceptance template for Gate D (one week).
- SRE/Infra: Prototype parser and schema conformance job (PR by end of sprint).

Appendix: quick parsing checklist for reviewers
- Confirm NDJSON is parseable with jq/python jsonlines.
- Look for presence of request_id, correlation_id, and timestamps in ISO-8601 with timezone.
- Verify that sensitive fields (PII) are redacted or hashed as agreed in the onboarding questionnaire.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep playbook lean; customers hate 50-step SOPs at first contact.
- Emphasize evidence artifacts — we can’t approve gates without artifacts captured.
- This doc should live alongside the onboarding runbook and link to the final PRD for private deployments.

---
Draft status: work-in-progress. Use this as a shared living doc during the next three onboarding engagements and iterate toward a formal PRD.
